title: Intermodulation and the two-tone test
idea: Overdrive an amplifier and two signals mix inside it. The odd-order products land right beside them, where no filter can help.

rows: Right next to F1 and F2

compare.how: Two signals mixing in a non-linear circuit, making unwanted outputs.
Mixing on purpose, in a mixer, to change frequency.
Two audio tones that aren't harmonically related, fed in to check the transmitter's linearity.

traps.why: Even-order products land far from the signals. The odd-order ones sit right beside them.
Add the multipliers: 3 + 1 = 4, even. 2F1 − F2 is 2 + 1 = 3, odd.
Heterodyning is mixing on purpose. Unwanted mixing in a non-linear stage is intermodulation.

traps.wrong: Two audio signals of the same frequency shifted 90 degrees
traps.why: Same frequency would be one tone. The test needs two different tones that aren't harmonically related.
It checks linearity: does a clean pair of tones come out as just a clean pair?
